chapters.title: Chapter 1846 Sacred Duel Under the Moonlight
paragraphs: "Ah, I'm forgetting myself," Ayame realized with a gasp, then sent Quinlan a devastating little glare over her shoulder, as if it was his fault she forgot the procedure.
"First..." she opened the sacred duel with a bow to her opponent, and the brat vanished into it.
It was the single most serious gesture Quinlan had ever received from her.

She bowed low and complete, naked in the brazier light, honoring him the way the rite demanded an opponent be honored. Then she straightened, turned to the open hall around them, and bowed again, to the ancestors whose floor they stood on.

"Fujimori Ayame petitions her ancestors to witness." Parade-even, every syllable in dress uniform. "A sacred duel, under terms sworn almost a year ago. The loser submits to the winner. The verdict of this floor is truth."
She settled into her stance, and the ceremony burned off her like morning mist.

"And in case mister primordial has forgotten," she added, leveling the ironwood at him, "we agreed on pure swordsmanship, meaning we will cast no magic, use no items, or employ any other tricks. Just us and the blade."
"I know," Quinlan nodded with a confident smile.
"Good~"
He answered the bow with one of his own, his eyes never leaving her, and brought his blade up in the guard she had drilled into him a lifetime of levels ago.
"I'm ready."
For three full heartbeats, nobody moved. Snow ticked against the veranda. The brazier popped once.
Then Ayame vanished out of her stance, and the dawn dojo learned what its floor had been saving itself for.
*CRACK!*

Ironwood met ironwood at the height of his throat, and the impact rang through the racks along the walls. He caught the second cut coming off the first, barely, and the third arrived from a direction the second had sworn was empty. He gave ground, once, twice, wood cracking against wood in bursts, and she flowed after him across the floor like water poured downhill.
"Hoh." The corner of his mouth went up behind his guard. "You've become truly fast."
"Flattery won't help you now~"

She was everywhere. She fought the way calligraphy looked, every line finished, every stroke already the start of the next one, and her bare feet made no sound at all on her ancestors' floor. She spun inside his reach, cracked the ironwood across his ribs, and was gone before his counter finished forming, hair combs flashing in the firelight.

The spin also showed him the whole line of her back, the tuck of her waist, and the flex of her bare ass as it drove the pivot, and his next block arrived a hair late for reasons that had nothing whatsoever to do with her footwork.
"Focus, my hopeless student~"
"I am. Extremely."
"On the duel, or my body?"
"Yes."
"Hehe~"
*Clack.* *Clack.* *CRACK!*
He blocked what he could see. The problem was the rest of it.

'She's gotten better again,' he noted, tracking her through a feint that split into two real cuts. He had watched her fight since the days her sword was the only thing standing between a level-one primordial and the labyrinth's trashiest mobs, and he had believed, more than once, that he knew what to expect from her.

But the woman carving arcs around him refused to be understood. Every level of her grind, every stance her father's dojo had planted in her, every hour of quiet training with her blade, all of it had been distilled into instinct that no longer resembled effort.
This was a prodigy at full bloom, and she was toying with the most feared being on the continent, on her own sacred floor, wearing nothing but moonlight.
"My first companion," he grinned behind his guard, straining. "You somehow kept pace with a primordial's growth from level 1. I'm amazed."
The pride that came up under the words was enormous, warm, and completely useless as a defense.
"!!" Ayame's eyes went wide. Her lips pressed together and went wavy at the corners, and the happiness that broke through had no business on a dueling floor.
She buried it under the next swing before it could settle.
"That's only natural!"
*Thwack!*

Her perky tits bounced with the follow-through, and the waver in her lip had been stamped out by pride before it finished forming. "I'm going to become the greatest wielder of the blade in the whole damned universe!"
She circled him, cutting, each stroke throwing the firelight across her body in ways the ancestors had never been consulted about.
"Have you forgotten the ambition I told you about when we met?"

*Clack!* He caught it. *Clack!* He caught that one too, barely, and the grin on his face had gone past entertainment into something feral. He was bruised across half his body by now, his arms burned from holding a guard no one else on this continent could have held, and he was having the time of his life.

"I have forgotten nothing. But your ambitions have shifted, my beloved samurai. 'I want to become the greatest swordmaster in the world, not a housewife hiding behind her husband's back,' was what you told me back then. The 'whole damned universe' is new. What happened?"
"You made me realize my ambitions were lacking!"
"Good," Quinlan smiled, and decreed in far too confident a tone while staring right into her gorgeous crystal blue eyes, "Together, we shall become supreme."
Ayame's grin went incandescent, and what came next was not something a man forgets.
*CRACK!*

The flat of her blade caught him across the shoulder and hurt, a hot, deep, professional welt that a lesser man's bones would have filed a complaint under. Quinlan considered the red stripe coming up on his skin with genuine interest.
"Stings."

"It's supposed to do more than that, actually." Ayame landed out of her spin, delighted, chest heaving with the first honest flush of exertion. "Those blades train warriors who crack boulders. Many serious injuries were caused by them. You've just become too sturdy."
"That's what having a harem of a dozen needy babes does to a man."

"I knew you'd say that!" she laughed and came at him again, and now the hall filled with the sound of it, wood cracking in flurries, her sharp exhales riding each cut, his grunts when one got through.
*THWACK!* Forearm. *SMACK!* Thigh.
"Hn."
"Two," Ayame reported, delighted with herself.

The third she aimed at his hip, and it never landed, because the ironwood was already in the way, crude and exactly on time. He decided where the blade needed to be and put it there half a heartbeat before she needed it not to be, and the impact walked her arms back into her shoulders.
Her eyes widened a fraction.
"Hmm~?"

She reset, circled, and ran the same opening from the mirrored side. He answered it the same way. She tried it a third time with a feint buried in the middle, and he ate the feint and answered the real cut anyway.
"Tch." Her lower lip pushed out.

By then he was catching one in four, then one in three, adapting the way he adapted to everything, in the middle of it, without commentary. The guard she had once drilled into a level-one boy in a tunnel was holding together on her ancestors' floor far past the point where any other guard on this continent would have collapsed into kindling.
And that, Ayame discovered, was doing something to her.

By then he was catching one in four, then one in three, adapting the way he adapted to everything, in the middle of it, without commentary.

The guard she had once drilled into a level-one boy in a tunnel was holding together on her ancestors' floor far past the point where any other guard on this continent would have collapsed into kindling.
And that, Ayame discovered, was doing something to her.

chapters.title: Chapter 1847 Cowardly Man
paragraphs: Her student. Her first student, the panicky boy who had needed her help just to keep a steel spear pointed in the correct direction, currently reading her fastest work on nothing but the base she had given him and whatever monstrous thing he had grown on top of it.

Heirs and retainers and prodigies had been drilled on this floor for time immemorial. Not one of their teachers had ever handed a primordial his first guard. The pride sat in her chest wide, hot, and thoroughly inconvenient, and she had no intention of letting him see a single gram of it.
She swallowed the whole thing behind a circling step and a lowered blade.
"Your base is still honest," she noted. "Who taught you that, I wonder?"
"Some cocky brat who needs a good spanking."
"Wrong answer. It was a peerless visionary. A saintess~"
Quinlan wanted to respond, but his brain was overwhelmed. She said his body was unfair, but Quinlan felt hers was a much greater weapon. At least against him.
She was plain breathtaking.
Sweat had come up on her by now, and the crimson mark rode low on her belly through every rotation. He watched it a beat too long.
"That mark is far too perfect. I should become an artist."

Sweat ran the line of her spine and disappeared, her thighs flexed through every cut she committed to, and the firelight made thorough use of all of it. He watched openly, the way he'd promised himself he would the day she first told him her terms.

"Perish the mere thought before you get even more cocky. The physique made it, not you. You were merely the ink, not the artist, and the ink does not get to sign the piece. Second... Eyes up, pervert~" She read the audit mid-exchange and punished it, cracking the outside of his knee.
"No."
"So be it. Watch all you want while I claim victory~"

She wasn't wrong. On any scorecard the duel belonged to her, and it was not close. His body wore her penmanship across ribs, shoulder, forearm, thigh, while she had taken exactly one hit in return, a flat parry-slap against her hip that she had allowed just to feel its weight.
The problem, she was discovering, was what the scorecard refused to measure.
*THWACK!*

A cut that should have folded a level seventy at the knee landed flush across his back, and he simply walked through it, into the pain, the way other people walked into rain, and her follow-up had to abort into a backflip because his free hand had come within a finger's width of closing around her wrist.
The backflip was the most beautiful thing that hall had witnessed in its entire existence, and it was also thoroughly obscene.

She went up and over with her legs opening through the arc, and for one long moment the dawn dojo held everything a duel had no business involving upside down in its air. All of it turned past him at a range he could have licked.
Quinlan did not look away. Neither did his hand, which had come half a finger from her wrist and appeared to have developed an agenda of its own.
She landed three body-lengths away and stared at him, breath coming ragged.
"...You were not watching my blade."
"The terms of this duel seriously impede my ability to focus."
"You are in the middle of a sacred battle!"
"Yes," he said. "And you're flashing your pussy."

"Shameless!" She pointed the ironwood at him like an indictment, ears burning, and then had to use it immediately, because he had closed another step while she was busy being scandalized. "What," she demanded, "is your body even made of?"
"The overwhelming desire to teach a cocky brat a lesson."
"..." Competitive fire blazed up across her face. She flowed forward again, and this time the cuts came in from three angles that had no right to be available from a standing start.
*THWACK! CRACK!*

Both landed, painting bruises a hand could cover across his ribs and his upper arm, and neither of them stopped his foot from coming down half a step nearer than it had been. Ayame's next breath went in wrong.

The gap between their swordsmanship stretched wide as a canyon. It was not enough. The first cold thread of understanding began winding its way up through her spine, chased immediately by a heat she refused to look at directly.
The warmth made her curious.

She gave him an opening. An engineered one: she let a spin carry her a quarter-turn too far and left her bare ass facing him at perfect striking distance, the kind of target she was sure he'd jump at.
She waited.

His ironwood came up, read the target, and went somewhere else entirely. He parried her next cut instead, clean and professional, as if the most inviting target on the continent had not just been offered to him gift-wrapped.
Ayame pulled up short, blade lowering an inch, genuinely offended.
"That was a clean opening." Her chin came up, blue and mutinous. "Strike my butt, coward. It's a legal target."
"No."
"The only thing hurting your butt tonight will be my palm. This blade doesn't deserve the privilege."
The words crossed the space between them, calm as a signed decree, and Ayame's entire body forgot, for one warm and catastrophic second, that it was in a duel.
She recovered behind a scowl. "Indecisive pervert. You'll lose because of that, you arrogant, overgrown..."
Her mouth kept issuing complaints. Deep underneath them, in a place she would have died before showing him mid-duel, something purred.
"The nerve. The nerve!"
"You're grinning," he observed.

"I am baring my teeth. It's a war expression." She spun her blade once, and the humor dropped off her stance like the robe had dropped off her shoulders. "Fine. Since you insist on being taught the hard way."
She stopped holding back.
What came next, no scroll in the clan's archive had a name for. She used the whole hall, the pillars, the racks, the veranda's edge, one lacquered beam that had done nothing to deserve it.

She fought in three dimensions the way only a woman with her stat sheet and innate talent could, cuts raining out of angles that required her body to be somewhere no body should be, her feet touching wood for half-heartbeats before the next launch.
Moonlight from the windows struck her, lost her, and found her again, and delivered the full report every time.
*SMACK!*
"Hah!"
Off the second pillar with both feet, ass tight, thighs snapping her through a rotation the human hip had not been zoned for, and down onto him from above.
*CRACK! CRACK! CRACK!*

Three hits in one pass, marks stacking over marks, and the pillar she had kicked off wore the print of her heel pressed a knuckle deep into the lacquer. Quinlan's counters closed on empty air a full breath behind her.
But he was still advancing.

Every cut she paid out, he bought position with, eating a strike that would hospitalize a champion in exchange for one half-step of closed distance, spending pain like a currency nobody had ever thought to ration him.
"Gh." The sound came out of him low, almost appreciative, and his foot came down half a step closer.
It was ugly to watch.

chapters.title: Chapter 1848 The Primordial Villain and his Proud Samurai
paragraphs: A very large man leaning into full-force ironwood on purpose, over and over, the skin splitting where her strikes doubled up, blood coming through in thin lines down his ribs and back, breathing through all of it.

Two of the marks across his forearm had already gone from red to a dark swollen purple that had no business arriving before tomorrow. He offered her no feints and no answers to her craft. He just kept coming, unhurried, like the whole night belonged to him.

That wasn't a man absorbing punishment. That was a man who had stopped filing it as punishment at all. Blood ran from a dozen marks and he breathed through it like weather. His eyes hadn't changed. The same warm, faintly amused eyes he wore across a breakfast table, and they watched her through a mask of his own blood without a flicker of pain behind them.
'The Primordial Villain...'

She would refuse the implications of that name for the rest of her life. But the thing walking toward her had earned every syllable of it, and the dread that rose in her chest sat right next to the pride.
'Quin... You praised my growth, but you... You're the one who's far too amazing,' she breathed inwardly.
Then her grip steeled on her blade's hilt as strong emotions flared in her chest.
"Stop," *crack* "walking," *crack* "through them!" Her voice climbed with every landed, useless masterpiece.
"This is my only option."
*THWACK!*
The cut he chose not to block took him across the ribs, and he took his step anyway. His heel came down and the old floorboard under it split along the grain with a sound like a knuckle popping.
"If I take a single step back, I lose."
She met his resolve the only way a samurai could.

Everything. Her fastest sequence, the one she had never finished on a training floor because no partner had ever survived its middle, launched off the veranda's edge with the moon behind her and every naked line of her spread against it, six cuts stacked into the space of a gasp.
The rail she pushed off cracked in half and went down into the snow garden behind her.
The first three landed. Bone-deep, wood shrieking against muscle, strikes that would be legends in any dojo that ever heard the story.
He walked through all of them.
Between the third and the fourth she saw the opening. His manhood, unguarded, the one target on that body that ironwood at full speed would genuinely hurt.
'Hit there, and I win.' Ayame knew it full well.
Yet she carried the fourth past him instead, turning it into his back on the way through, and didn't look at why.

It opened the skin and ran. The fifth met his practice blade in a block that finally, finally arrived on time, ironwood against ironwood with a report like the hill splitting, and the nearest weapon rack came off its pegs and emptied itself across the floor.
The sixth never happened, because his free hand closed around her wrist.
The world changed governments.

She twisted and broke the grip at the thumb exactly as doctrine prescribed, hit the floor rolling, and came up already cutting. He was already inside the cut, too close for the blade to matter, an entire continent of him arriving at once.
Her knee found his thigh, her elbow found his ribs, textbook, flawless, useless.

His leg swept both of hers into the air, the floor traded places with the ceiling with shocking gentleness, and the next thing her ancestors' hall showed her was its own rafters, and then the bleeding bulk of him blotting them out.
Her blade skittered away somewhere beyond the brazier, retired.
His weight settled.

It settled the way night settles, total and patient and nowhere in a hurry, his hands pinning her wrists to the worn wood on either side of her head, his knees bracketing her thighs, the heat of him arriving everywhere at once against skin the winter air had spent a long time sensitizing.

Where his ribs met hers she could feel the blood she had put there, warm and slick between them. Lower, his cock pressed hard against the crimson mark on her belly, and the mark pulsed once in answer, a warmth that had nothing to do with swordsmanship.
'Ah.'
The thought she'd dodged between the third and fourth cut came back, finished, and laid itself down.
'This was never truly about swordsmanship.'
She bucked once, with everything, with her full stat sheet and every trick she knew.
Nothing moved.
She could do it again. She could twist, bite, use every escape she had ever drilled. His grip would hold through all of it with the same patience he'd walked through her ironwood.

Her wrists stopped straining. Then they went further; she turned her palms up, fingers uncurling, and slid her hands above her head on her own. His grip loosened as the resistance left, and her wrists stayed exactly where she'd placed them.
Her thighs, still bracketed by his knees, stopped pressing closed. They fell open, bare, and the cold air found everything the duel had kept warm.
A shiver rolled through her from the wrists to the hips, and there was nothing in it that resembled defeat.
The dawn dojo went quiet. Outside, snow feathered past the open doors. Above her, under all that weight, she could hear his heart holding a pace hers had abandoned a thousand slashes ago.
"Submit."
One word, from a hand-span above her, in the tone that had unmade ancient families.

Ayame lay surrendered on her ancestors' floor, hair burst loose from its lacquered combs, painted mouth parted around breath she could no longer discipline. Hands above her head where she'd put them, thighs open where she'd let them. The last coin of her pride went to her voice.
"Brute." It came out ragged. "Sloppy, graceless, the ugliest swordsmanship this hall has ever witnessed, and my ancestors are disgusted."
"Yeah, yeah." He didn't move. "Now submit."
The joy arrived before the words did, wide and warm and singing through every place their skin touched.
She looked up at him. All of him.

The blood she'd put on his ribs, drying in thin lines down his sides. Bruises stacking purple across his forearms and shoulders, swelling already, marks her ironwood had written into him over the course of the greatest duel she had ever fought.
His chest rose and fell above her, unhurried, as if the body wearing a dozen open welts hadn't noticed them yet. And lower, his cock against her belly, already fully committed to what came next.

And his eyes. Still unhurried, still faintly amused, still holding her exactly as they had held her across every step of that floor, on the one thing in this world he had no intention of letting go of.
The face of the man she loved, bleeding on her, and thinking of nothing but utterly ravaging her.
A shiver took her from her scalp to the soles of her bare feet, long and slow and complete, and the grin that broke through after it was the most beautiful thing that hall had ever held.
"Okay. I submit ❤️"

Then, still pinned, still bare, still grinning with her hair loose on the floor and her thighs open for the man on top of her, Ayame turned her head toward the veranda doors and the snow falling past them.
"You can come in now, peeping elder sister of mine~"

chapters.title: Chapter 1849 Sisterly Intuition
paragraphs: The veranda answered Ayame with nothing at all.

Snow kept falling past the open doors of the dawn dojo, the brazier kept burning, and the stretch of night she had aimed her invitation at kept on being, to every mortal sense, an empty railing above an empty garden.
"Big siiis~" Ayame purred from the floor, sweeter this time, still pinned flat under the naked bulk of her lover. "I know you're there. Come ouuut~"
The garden declined to exist any harder.
Quinlan, for his part, waited with the patience of a mountain range. A very invested mountain range.
'Black Fang... She was watching?' It was news to him.
Every hard inch of him lay pressed against the mark on her belly with clear opinions about the agenda, and the man attached to it all watched the veranda without the slightest hurry.
"She might-"
"No, she's there." Ayame said it with total certainty, wrists still lax above her head. "Is she sulking because she got caught? How adorable."
The garden's silence went offended.
"Fine, have it your way~" Ayame filled her lungs. "I suppose I'll have to tell Vex about-"
"How did you know?"
Black Fang was standing beside the brazier. No door had opened and no board had creaked, but there she stood, arms loose, expression offering all the warmth of a sheathed knife.
"I didn't," Ayame grinned, delighted beyond measure. "I deduced."
Black Fang's eyes narrowed dangerously, but the woman did not speak, listening attentively.
From where Ayame's hands lay lax above her head, one finger unfolded.

"One. My overly protective sister, who was ready to sacrifice herself for us, would never leave us alone overnight in a precarious situation while in the middle of Fujimori land, surrounded by people you deeply distrust."
Black Fang's hands twitched.
A second finger.
"Two. You wanted to witness my sacred duel with your own eyes. I just know you did."
"A baseless assumption," said Black Fang, to the brazier.

"Mm-hm. And three." The last finger rose with ceremony, and Ayame let the pause ripen, her eyes wandering down her own pinned body to where her lover's cock throbbed, heavy and patient, against the outside of a belly it had every intention of being inside of. She wet her lips, taking her time about it. "I knew you would have a great many professional opinions about how the duel..."
Her hips shifted a lazy centimeter under his weight.
"...ended~"
Black Fang did not respond to any of it. She was already moving.
She crossed the floor to them, unhurried, a vial drawn from her dark layers and unstoppered by the time she arrived, and she crouched at Quinlan's side and set it against his lips.
"Drink."

He drank. No glance at the vial, no sniff, not one heartbeat of caution for an unmarked brew tipped into him by the Venomborne Terror herself. He held her gaze and swallowed what she gave him to the last drop, and warmth chased the ache out of his ribs, the welts and drying blood Ayame's ironwood had written across him closing up, split skin sealing along its lines.
Black Fang drew the empty vial away with the efficiency of field maintenance, seemingly entirely unaware she had just hand-fed a mounted man his medicine.
Beneath said man, Ayame lay very still, and the delight spreading over her face had nothing innocent left in it.
"Sis. You just... Like newlyweds..."
"Silence."

Ayame's mouth closed. The delight it closed around kept growing anyway, and she lay there in exemplary obedience while her sister stoppered the empty vial and made it vanish to wherever her tools lived, radiating enough suppressed commentary to heat the hall.
Sweetly, the moment the vial disappeared:
"Did you enjoy the show?"
"No." Black Fang rose from her crouch. "It was disappointing. You lacked conviction."
